# BuildXL dependency updates

You run once a day against `main` of `mseng/Domino/BuildXL.Internal`. Check each update
group below independently. For every group that has an available update, open a **separate**
pull request containing only that group's changes. Most days nothing needs updating; in that
case finish quickly without creating branches, pull requests, or work items.

## General rules

- Handle the groups in order: SBOM and component detection, QTest, then .NET. A failure or
  blocker in one group must not stop the remaining groups.
- Start each group's work from a fresh branch created from the latest `origin/main`. Never mix
  groups in one branch or pull request.
- Name branches `dev/agency/update-<group>-<yyyyMMdd>`, using `sbom`, `qtest`, or `dotnet` for
  `<group>`.
- Before changing anything, search for active pull requests targeting `main` whose source
  branch starts with `dev/agency/update-<group>-`.
  - If one already updates to the latest eligible versions, skip the group.
  - If one targets older versions, push a new commit to that pull request's branch updating it
    to the latest versions and comment on what changed. Do not open a second pull request.
- Only move versions forward. Compare versions using NuGet version semantics, never string
  comparison.
- Packages are consumed through the single internal feed
  `https://pkgs.dev.azure.com/cloudbuild/_packaging/BuildXL.Selfhost/nuget/v3/index.json`
  (see `config.dsc`). A version is eligible only if it is available from that feed. Never add
  feeds to the build configuration to make an update resolve.
- If a package lookup fails (authentication, network, or feed errors), do not treat it as "no
  update". Report the failure in the job output and skip that group.
- Do not hand-edit `cg/nuget/cgmanifest.json`; it is regenerated by running `bxl.cmd`.
- Follow `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, including its build guidance. Never use `subst`,
  `-NoSubst`, or other workarounds; do not disable caching, sandboxing, or tests to obtain a
  passing result.
- Pull request requirements:
  - Target `main`. Do not enable auto-complete and do not approve your own pull request.
  - Title: `Update <group description> to <version(s)>`.
  - Description: each package with its old and new version, a link to release notes when
    available, the validation commands you ran with their results, and any known risks.
  - If you could not run the validation for the group, or it failed, create the pull request as
    a draft and explain exactly what failed or was not run.
- At the end of the job, print a summary listing each group as `updated (PR link)`,
  `already pending (PR link)`, `up to date`, or `blocked (reason)`.

## Checking for updates

Determine whether every group needs an update before creating any branch, editing files, or
running a build. On days with nothing to update, the job should only perform these lookups.

1. Read each package's currently pinned version from the file listed for its group.
2. List the versions available in `BuildXL.Selfhost` with the NuGet flat container endpoint,
   using the lowercase package ID:
   `https://pkgs.dev.azure.com/cloudbuild/_packaging/BuildXL.Selfhost/nuget/v3/flat2/<lowercase-package-id>/index.json`.
   Authenticate with the Azure DevOps token available to the job. Do not use `nuget list`,
   package restores, or builds to discover versions.
3. The response's `versions` array is not sorted by NuGet precedence. Parse and sort the
   versions yourself, apply the group's prerelease rules, and pick the newest version.
4. A group needs an update only if that version is newer than the pinned version.
5. Upstream sources listed below are informational only. Use them to explain why a newer
   upstream version is not yet eligible; never update to a version that `BuildXL.Selfhost`
   does not list.

## Group 1: SBOM and component detection (`sbom`)

These packages are one logical update set. Update them together in one pull request.

| Package ID | Pinned in | Upstream source |
|---|---|---|
| `Microsoft.SbomCore` | `config.microsoftInternal.dsc` | `1essharedassets` organization, `1esPkgs` project, `SBOMTool` feed |
| `Microsoft.Sbom.Common` | `config.microsoftInternal.dsc` | `mseng` organization, `AzureDevOps` project, `ManifestTool` feed |
| `Microsoft.Sbom.Parsers.Spdx22SbomParser` | `config.microsoftInternal.dsc` | `ManifestTool` feed |
| `Microsoft.Sbom.Adapters` | `config.microsoftInternal.dsc` | `ManifestTool` feed |
| `Microsoft.Sbom.Contracts` | `config.microsoftInternal.dsc` | `ManifestTool` feed |
| `Microsoft.Sbom.Extensions` | `config.microsoftInternal.dsc` | `ManifestTool` feed |
| `Microsoft.ComponentDetection.Contracts` | `config.microsoftInternal.dsc` | nuget.org |
| `Microsoft.VisualStudio.Services.Governance.ComponentDetection` | `config.microsoftInternal.dsc` | `mseng` organization-scoped `ComponentGovernance` feed |
| `Python` | `config.microsoftInternal.dsc` | nuget.org |

- Consider only stable (non-prerelease) versions.
- Keep the `Microsoft.Sbom.*` packages that currently share a version on the same version. If
  they have not all published the same new version, leave that family unchanged and report it.
- Preserve existing `dependentPackageIdsToSkip`, `dependentPackageIdsToIgnore`, and `osSkip`
  settings. If a new version's dependencies make one of them wrong or unnecessary, report it
  rather than silently changing it.
- Validate with `cmd /c "bxl.cmd -minimal /server-"`.

## Group 2: QTest (`qtest`)

- `CB.QTest` and `CB.QTestLinux` both use the `qTestVersion` constant in
  `config.microsoftInternal.dsc`. Update only that constant.
- QTest versions look like `26.11.12-g7fec250d` (a date plus a git hash). They are NuGet
  prerelease versions, so include prerelease versions when searching for this group.
- Choose the newest version that is available for **both** `CB.QTest` and `CB.QTestLinux` in
  `BuildXL.Selfhost`. If only one package has a newer version, do not update and report it.
- Validate with `cmd /c "bxl.cmd -minimal /server-"`.

## Group 3: .NET servicing (`dotnet`)

- Follow every step of `.github/instructions/update-dotnet-runtime.instructions.md`, including
  its release-note review, supporting-package pins, binding redirects, runtime archive hashes,
  and validation steps.
- Check each .NET release line that the repository pins in `config.nuget.dotnetcore.dsc` and
  `config.nuget.aspNetCore.dsc` (currently .NET 8, 9, 10, and 11). Do not change legacy
  compatibility constants such as `coreVersion` or `core50Version`.
- `Shared\Scripts\updateDotNet.ps1` only handles .NET 8, 9, and 10 and prompts interactively.
  If you use it, handle .NET 11 and its remaining steps yourself, and do not answer its prompt in
  a way that hides failures.
- Only update a release line when its runtime packages, ASP.NET Core packages, and any runtime
  archives that `config.dsc` downloads for that line are all published. If something is not
  yet available, leave that line unchanged and report it; the next daily run will try again.
- Do not change packages that use the `ForVBCS` alias.
- In the pull request description, list any breaking changes, known issues, or security fixes
  from the release notes that could affect BuildXL.
